He did it by thinking in decades, not quarters. From a failed social app in his 20s to leading OpenAI, his entire arc shows a single trait: clarity. At Y Combinator, he didn’t just fund great companies. He pattern-matched great founders. He once said: “The best founders aren’t the smartest. Study the systems thinker behind it. …more 157 4 Comments Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X Transcript Transcript Transcript Meet the founder Sam Altman. You've probably used his product this week, maybe even today, but you might not have heard this about him. And no, he didn't start with a billion dollar idea. He started with an app that told your friends where you were. But the founder who built and failed location app in his 20s now runs the company trying to control artificial intelligence. Meet Sam Altman At 27 years old, Sam Altman became the president of Why Combinator, the startup accelerator behind Airbnb, Stripe and Dropbox. But here's the part that most people miss. He didn't just fund great companies, he patterned matched great founders. He once said the best founders are clear thinkers who act fast, Not necessarily the smartest, but the clearest. And when it came to building open AI, he didn't chase virality. He quietly assembled a team of elite researchers and created a nonprofit to make sure that a I wouldn't destroy us. And that didn't exactly go as planned. Altman isn't your typical Silicon Valley showman. He's a systems thinker obsessed with existential risk. Geopolitics in the. Idea that intelligence, not code, is the most powerful force on earth. If you're building anything in tech, you should study Sam. Not because he went viral, but because he plays in decades, not quarters. Shirley Jean-Baptiste, MS 10mo Report this comment Same guy responsible for the obliteration of millions of jobs.
